claims.hypothesis: Can MHD wind-driven accretion reproduce the AGE-PRO disk populations together with disk fraction and accretion rates?
claims.experiment: Sequentially fit disk fraction and Lupus accretion rate, CO size and gas mass with synthetic populations, then compare with Ophiuchus and Upper Sco
claims.result: Best-fit populations with R0 about 10 au, omega 0.25-0.5 and low f_M match all three regions, omega = 0.5 doing slightly better
claims.finding: MHD wind-driven accretion with compact disks and beta about 1e5 matches the bulk properties of the populations

evidence.quote: MHD wind-driven accretion can reproduce the bulk properties of the disk populations from Ophiuchus to Upper Sco assuming compact disks with an initial magnetization of about $\beta \simeq 10^5$

claims.hypothesis: Can turbulence-driven accretion with internal photoevaporation reproduce disk fraction and CO sizes?
claims.experiment: Constrain mass-loss rate, initial mass, size and viscous timescale with disk fraction, Lupus accretion rate and CO size
claims.result: Compact initial disks (R0 5-20 au) with long viscous timescales (0.4-3 Myr) fit disk fraction and gas sizes
claims.finding: Turbulence-driven models can reproduce disk fraction and gas sizes but not simultaneously the disk masses

evidence.quote: turbulence-driven accretion with initially compact disks ($R_0 \simeq 5-20~$au), low mass-loss rates, and relatively long viscous timescales ($t_{\nu,0} \simeq 0.4-3~$Myr or $\alpha_{SS} \simeq 2-4 \times 10^{-4}$) can reproduce the disk fraction and gas sizes.

claims.hypothesis: Do turbulence-driven models reproduce the observed apparent disk lifetime M_D/Mdot?
claims.experiment: Compare the M_D-Mdot plane and cumulative distribution of M_D/Mdot for the best-fit populations with the AGE-PRO sources
claims.result: Turbulence-driven populations give M_D/Mdot longer than about the disk age, while half the AGE-PRO sample is below 1 Myr
claims.finding: Turbulence-driven models overestimate the apparent disk lifetime; MHD wind-driven models match it

evidence.quote: However, the distribution of apparent disk lifetime defined as the $M_D/\dot{M}_*$ ratio is severely overestimated by turbulence-driven models.

claims.hypothesis: Is the tension with turbulence-driven models robust to the AGE-PRO disk mass estimates?
claims.experiment: Discuss how a systematic underestimate of disk masses would change the fits
claims.result: If masses were underestimated by a factor of five to ten, turbulence-driven models would be compatible with the data
claims.finding: The tension depends on the low gas masses, notably of compact disks, which need confirmation

evidence.quote: If disk masses in these regions were to be systematically underestimated by a factor of five to ten, turbulence-driven models would be compatible with the data
More studies are needed to confirm the low masses found by AGE-PRO

claims.hypothesis: Does disk dispersal bias the evolution of median population properties?
claims.experiment: Track initial properties of surviving disks in best-fit populations
claims.result: Dispersal removes light disks (turbulent) or compact disks (MHD), flattening median mass or raising median CO size
claims.finding: Survivorship bias must be included when interpreting survey medians

evidence.loc: 4.4 Disk dispersal and the survivorship bias

limitations_admitted.value: External photoevaporation and multiplicity are neglected; Upper Sco is the only old-region reference

evidence.quote: We further neglect the impact of mild external UV irradiation
In our models, we neglect the effect of multiplicity

referee_caveats_inferred: Best-fit parameters come from a manual sequential grid search without uncertainties, so quoted ranges are not confidence intervals and depend on stage order
Only 30 AGE-PRO disks (about 10 per region) with large mass uncertainties (0.7 dex) constrain the medians
Fixed spreads and no correlations between parameters are assumed; other choices could change the survivor-biased medians
Ophiuchus is treated as t=0 although its masses use a different method
Model R_CO,90% uses an analytical column-density criterion, not radiative transfer
Photoevaporation profile rests on a single hydrodynamical model; MHD model assumes constant lambda and a parameterized field decline (omega)

missing_for_reproduction: Numerical values of the observed medians, spreads and per-source data used as targets (figure only)
Diskpop and Popcorn versions and exact configuration files, grids and random seeds
Selection criterion for the best-fit models within the allowed region
Photoevaporation mass-loss profile file and fixed lambda values for MHD runs
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Negligible: no ALMA visibilities processed; uses published AGE-PRO derived quantities and model runs of 400 disks per population
reproducibility.score_reason: Model equations, fitting stages, tolerances and many numeric results are given and the Diskpop code is cited, but observed target medians appear only in figures and software settings, versions and the best-fit selection rule are not stated.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper states no data release or code release for these fits, the observational targets are only in companion papers or figures, and the best-fit selection is manual.
